info.bio: La banda de rock alternativo Curve surge en Londres en 1991 alrededor de la cantante Toni Halliday y el guitarrista Dean Garcia tras la desaparición de una banda anterior, State of Play. Publicaron numerosos EPs que se convirtieron en éxitos indie por su sonido inflamado, orientado al noise-pop. scenes.name: Psicodelia británica de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La edad de oro de la psicodelia británica no fueron los sesenta sino los noventa: las raves crean una demanda inagotable de música inducida por (o para) las drogas. La versión pop (Telescopes, Inspiral Carpets, Verve, Sundial, Auteurs, Kula Shaker), las más sofisticadas (Curve, Cranberries, Rollerskate Skinny, Beta Band, dEUS, Gorky's Zygotic Mynci), el space-rock libre (Porcupine Tree, Terminal Cheesecake, Heads), los últimos shoegazers (Ride, Swervedriver, Spectrum y E.A.R. de Sonic Boom, Spiritualized de Jason Pierce, Flying Saucer Attack, encuentro de shoegazing y ambient) y el dream-pop (Lush, Pale Saints, Slowdive, Catherine Wheel, Bark Psychosis).

podcast.title: Breakups and Reunions
podcast.body: Curve initially disbanded in 1994. However, they later reunited in 1996 and continued to perform together for approximately ten years before once again going their separate ways. "They broke up in 1994, got together again for about 10 years, starting in 1996, before they once again went their separate ways."

podcast.body: Curve was mentioned as an example of a Shoegaze band, a style known for its performers' habit of avoiding audience contact by staring at the floor, which gave the genre its name. "There were bands like Slow Dive, Chapter House, Curve, Lush, My Bloody Valentine, Adorable, The Catherine Wheel."

xref.title: Supergroup Lineup and Origins (1994-2001)
xref.body: Tapeworm was conceived as a side project during Nine Inch Nails' "The Downward Spiral" sessions in 1994, intended as a collaborative effort for Danny Lohner and Charlie Clouser. It evolved to include a star-studded lineup: Trent Reznor, Maynard James Keenan (Tool), producer Alan Molder, Atticus Ross, Phil Anselmo and Rex Brown (Pantera), Page Hamilton (Helmet), Toni Halliday (Curve), Tommy Victor (Ministry), and drummer Josh Freese, with at least an album's worth of material recorded by 2001. "If you're Trent Rezner, Danny Loaner and Charlie Closer from his live band, Maynard James Keenan from Tool, producer Alan Molder and Atticus Ross. I mean, wow, awesome, right? The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Tapeworm was designed as something to which Danny and Charlie could contribute as equals. This idea evolved into something pretty cool. Maynard was brought in, Phil and Salmo from Pantera, Paige Hamilton from Helmut, Tony Haliday from a cool band called Curve, Tommy Victor from Ministry, drummer Josh Freeze. And then in 2001, Alan Molder apparently helped record at least an album's worth of stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Project History (1995-2004)
xref.body: This project was created in 1995 and involved Trent Reznor, Atticus Ross, and a variety of friends, continuing off and on for nine years. Despite the collaboration, nothing was ever officially released. "I already mentioned the tapeworm project, which was created in 1995 and included a lot of different friends. They were continued off and on for nine years, but nothing was ever released."

xref.title: Evolving Sound
xref.body: Queens of the Stone Age is known for taking chances and risks with each new record, actively avoiding repetition and embracing a "curve ball" approach to their sound. This commitment to change means fans never quite know what to expect, and the constantly shifting lineup contributes to this sonic evolution. "The last thing Josh Hommie and whatever his crew is in Queen of the Stone Age want to do is repeat themselves."

xref.title: Experimental Progressive Rock
xref.body: Radiohead was highlighted for their experimental approach and their continuous effort to "stay ahead of the curve" within the 2010s progressive rock comeback. Their unique methods were a significant part of this broad movement that valued an "attitude and an approach to instruments and arrangements." "And amongst all of them was radiohead, with their experimental ways, always trying to stay ahead of the curve."

xref.title: Inventor of the Archtop Guitar
xref.body: Orville Gibson invented the Archtop guitar, which features a slight arch or curve on the front of the guitar's body. He derived this design principle from the construction of violins. "Orville then invented the Archtop guitar. This means the front of the guitar's body has a slight arch accurve to it. Orville got this idea from how violins are constructed."

xref.title: Marfan Syndrome
xref.body: He had Marfan Syndrome, a genetic connective tissue disorder that accounted for his tall, spindly physique and curved spine. "as well as a genetic condition of the body's connected tissue called Marfan Syndrome. This explains why he was so tall and spindly and had the curve spine."

xref.body: USS's first EP, "From Welding the Sea Drive," released years before, contained sounds and styles that were similar to what Twenty One Pilots would later achieve, implying USS was ahead of the curve.
